text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unofficial presidential election results are showing that Tudjman has captured 61.4 percent of the vote.
- Economy ministers of Croatia and Slovenia Nenad Porges and Metod Dragonja, express optimism during discussions on the ways of resolving the Krsko nuclear power plant joint ownership problems.
- An analysis of the elections points to Tudjman's popularity rising by five percent in comparison to what it was in the first presidential elections.
- The OSCE monitors claim the Croatian elections were free, but unfair.
- Gotovac HSLS presidential election team is disappointed at not securing the second round of elections and worried about the absence of voters.
- The average wage for April was 2,591 kuna, up 95 kuna in comparison to March wages. The highest wages were received by bankers and insurers.
- Insurers to attempt to sever a fraud chain that enables those with bogus spine injuries to get up to 50,000 kuna in damages.
- Capital market: Tourist groups' shares have reached rock bottom over the past week.
- Croatian police are surfing the net in their bid to crack down on comptuer hackers as new articles on computer fraud are to be added to the penal code.
- Refugee status to be revoked for displaced people from all the reconstructed villages in Dalmatia and also the areas in Banovina and Kordun where reconstruction efforts have been completed.
- Dubrovnik returns as a destination for big tourst cruise ships. July is to see the sailing in of eight and August of 10 such vessels.
- According to a Slovene polling agency some 50 percent of Slovenes will spend their holidays in Croatia. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
